A classic puzzle cuts an 8×8 square (area 64) into 4 pieces and rearranges them into a 5×13 rectangle (area 65) — using the exact same four pieces. Since area cannot actually appear from nowhere, what is really going on?
choices: One of the four pieces is quietly resized between the two arrangements.
The four pieces don't perfectly form a true rectangle — a thin sliver-shaped gap along the diagonal, invisible at normal drawing scale, accounts for the 'missing' unit of area.
Area is not conserved when flat shapes are cut and rigidly rearranged.
The original square doesn't actually measure exactly 8×8; rounding in the drawing causes the discrepancy.

questions.q: Cheryl tells Albert and Bernard that her birthday is one of: May 15, May 16, May 19, June 17, June 18, July 14, July 16, August 14, August 15, August 17. She tells Albert only the month and Bernard only the day. Albert says: 'I don't know when Cheryl's birthday is, but I know Bernard doesn't know either.' Bernard then says: 'At first I didn't know, but now I do.' Albert then says: 'Now I know too.' What is Cheryl's birthday?

In a single round of the Prisoner's Dilemma, two purely rational, self-interested players cannot communicate or retaliate later. Mutual cooperation would leave both better off than mutual defection. What does classical game theory say two such rational players will actually do?
choices: Each randomizes 50/50 between cooperating and defecting
They split — one cooperates while the other defects
Both will cooperate, since cooperation is the jointly optimal choice
Both will defect — defection dominates cooperation for each player individually, even though it leaves them both worse off
